title: Law of the finite-family Fourier estimator
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a target function, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\varepsilon$ be a rational learning parameter with $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12$. The estimator program's outcome law is the law obtained by drawing an independent uniform batch of the prescribed sample size for each $S\in\mathcal F$ and returning the hypothesis whose coefficient at $S$ is the empirical Fourier coefficient from that batch.
hypotheses_covered: target Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
